Given:

Rate (R) = 5% per annum

Time (T)= 2 years

Difference between C.I and S.I = ₹152

Formula Used:

Simple Interest = (P × R × T)/100

Compound Interest = P[(1 + (R)/(100))T- 1]

Where, P = Principal

R = rate

T = Time

Calculation:

According to question,

S.I for 2 years = (P × 5 × 2)/100

⇒ ₹(10P)/100 ----1

C.I for 2 years = P[(1 + (5)/(100))² -1]

⇒ P[(21/20)² - 1]

⇒ P[(441/400) - 1]

⇒ P(41/400) ----2

Now as per question,

Difference between C.I and S.I = ₹152 

Substracting equation (1) by (2)

P(41/400) - 10P/100 = ₹152

P(41-40)/400 = ₹152

P/400 = ₹152

P = ₹60,800

∴ The amount (in ₹) is 60,800.
